name: christianpure-jerusalem-sky
title: The sky over Jerusalem: months, Passover and eclipses, 1000 BC to AD 135
description: When each Hebrew month most likely began, by crescent sighting from the Temple Mount, for all 14,038 months from 1000 BC to AD 135; the date and weekday of Passover (14 and 15 Nisan) for every year under two month-start rules; every lunar eclipse and every solar eclipse seen at Jerusalem, Samaria or Nineveh from 1999 BC to AD 500; and the sky on named nights (the Star of Bethlehem candidates, AD 30 and AD 33, 15 June 763 BC, Paul's voyage). From JPL DE441 through Skyfield, with Yallop's crescent test and the Delta T margin on every row. Julian calendar, with Julian Day Numbers. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0.

sources.title: JPL planetary and lunar ephemeris DE441: Park, R. S., Folkner, W. M., Williams, J. G., and Boggs, D. H. 2021. The JPL Planetary and Lunar Ephemerides DE440 and DE441. Astronomical Journal 161:105
Skyfield 1.55, Brandon Rhodes (Astrophysics Source Code Library ascl:1907.024)
Yallop, B. D. 1997. A Method for Predicting the First Sighting of the New Crescent Moon. NAO Technical Note 69, HM Nautical Almanac Office
Morrison, L. V., and Stephenson, F. R. 2004. Historical values of the Earth's clock error Delta T and the calculation of eclipses. Journal for the History of Astronomy 35:327-336 (the Delta T margin)

Morrison, L. V., Stephenson, F. R., Hohenkerk, C. Y., and Zawilski, M. 2021. Addendum 2020 to Measurement of the Earth's rotation: 720 BC to AD 2015. Proceedings of the Royal Society A 477:20200776 (Delta T itself, as Skyfield uses it)
Stephenson, F. R., Morrison, L. V., and Hohenkerk, C. Y. 2016. Measurement of the Earth's rotation: 720 BC to AD 2015. Proceedings of the Royal Society A 472:20160404 (Delta T before 720 BC)
Espenak, F., and Meeus, J. Five Millennium Canon of Lunar Eclipses and Five Millennium Catalog of Moon Phases, NASA (the checks)

fields.name: delta_t_s
fields.description: Delta T used (TT minus UT), in seconds, as Skyfield gives it.

fields.name: delta_t_sigma_s
fields.description: Standard error of Delta T in seconds, 0.8 t^2 with t in centuries from 1820 (Morrison and Stephenson 2004).

fields.description: Moon's age at sunset on that evening, in hours from the new moon.

fields.name: eve1_lag_min
fields.description: Minutes from sunset to moonset that evening (negative when the moon set first).

fields.name: eve1_q
fields.description: Yallop's q value at his best time for sighting (sunset plus four-ninths of the lag).

fields.name: eve1_grade
fields.description: Yallop's visibility grade: A easily seen by eye, B seen by eye in perfect conditions, C may need optical aid to find, then seen by eye, D needs optical aid, E not visible with a telescope, F not visible (the moon sets before the sun or is below Danjon's limit).

fields.description: Likely start: the first evening graded A or B. The month begins at sunset that evening, so day 1 is the next daylight day. Civil date, Julian calendar, astronomers' year numbering (1 BC is 0000, 2 BC is -0001), written YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: likely_margin
fields.description: Empty when the likely start is firm. Otherwise says in words why it could move a night: moving Delta T by twice its standard error, or the 30-day rule.

resources.description: One row per eclipse per place, 1999 BC to AD 500.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: solar or lunar.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Type of eclipse: for lunar, Total, Partial or Penumbral as seen from Earth; for solar, the type seen at this place (Total, Annular, Partial).

fields.name: year
fields.description: Year in astronomers' numbering: 1 BC is 0, 2 BC is -1, AD 1 is 1.

fields.name: year_label
fields.description: The same year written for readers, BC or AD.

fields.name: greatest_ut_date
fields.description: Date of greatest eclipse in Universal Time. Civil date, Julian calendar, astronomers' year numbering (1 BC is 0000, 2 BC is -0001), written YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: greatest_ut_date_jdn
fields.description: Julian Day Number of `greatest_ut_date` (the day that begins at noon UT on that date): one count of days with no calendar to doubt.

fields.name: greatest_ut
fields.description: Time of greatest eclipse, UT, HH:MM. For a solar eclipse, greatest as seen at this place.

fields.name: greatest_jd_ut
fields.description: Greatest eclipse as a Julian Date in UT.

fields.name: delta_t_s
fields.description: Delta T used, seconds.

fields.name: delta_t_2sigma_s
fields.description: Twice the standard error of Delta T, seconds: the margin each way.

fields.name: place_id
fields.description: Place ID in the bible-places folder of this repository.

fields.name: place
fields.description: Place name: Jerusalem, Samaria or Nineveh.

fields.name: greatest_local
fields.description: Greatest eclipse at the place. Local mean time at the place, Julian calendar, astronomers' years: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.

fields.name: phase_start_local
fields.description: Start of the umbral phase (lunar) or first contact (solar). Local mean time at the place, Julian calendar, astronomers' years: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.

fields.name: phase_end_local
fields.description: End of the umbral phase (lunar) or last contact (solar). Local mean time at the place, Julian calendar, astronomers' years: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.

fields.name: magnitude
fields.description: Lunar: umbral magnitude (share of the moon's diameter inside Earth's dark shadow; 1 or more is total; negative for penumbral eclipses). Solar: share of the sun's diameter covered at this place.

fields.name: penumbral_magnitude
fields.description: Lunar only: penumbral magnitude.

fields.name: magnitude_dt_low
fields.description: Solar only: magnitude at the place with Delta T moved down by twice its standard error.

fields.name: magnitude_dt_high
fields.description: Solar only: magnitude with Delta T moved up by twice its standard error.

fields.name: body_alt_at_greatest_dt_low
fields.description: Height of the moon (lunar) or sun (solar) above the horizon at greatest, degrees, Delta T low.

fields.name: body_alt_at_greatest_dt_mid
fields.description: The same with the usual Delta T.

fields.name: body_alt_at_greatest_dt_high
fields.description: The same with Delta T high.

fields.name: visible_dt_low
fields.description: yes if any of the eclipse could be seen from the place, Delta T low.

fields.name: visible_dt_mid
fields.description: The same with the usual Delta T.

fields.name: visible_dt_high
fields.description: The same with Delta T high.

fields.name: minutes_visible_dt_low
fields.description: Minutes of the eclipse with the body above the horizon (lunar: umbral phase, moon up and sun down), Delta T low.

fields.name: minutes_visible_dt_mid
fields.description: The same with the usual Delta T.

fields.name: minutes_visible_dt_high
fields.description: The same with Delta T high.

fields.name: first_seen_local
fields.description: When the eclipse could first be seen, usual Delta T. Local mean time at the place, Julian calendar, astronomers' years: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.

fields.name: sun_alt_when_first_seen
fields.description: Height of the sun at that moment, degrees (lunar: shows whether the sky was still light).
